#Part 1
1.Open the sleep dataset in R
```{r}
data("sleep")
```


2. Is it long or wide format? How do you know?
```{r}
#long. It has a fewer columns and more rows. It contains multiple rows per participant.
```


3. Transform this data so that it is in the other format.
```{r}
sleepwide<- pivot_wider(sleep, id_cols = "ID", names_from = "group", values_from = "extra")
sleepwide


```

4. Transform your data back to its original format.
```{r}


sleepLongAgain<- pivot_longer(sleepwide, cols = c("1", "2"), names_to = "group", values_to = "extra")
sleepLongAgain

```

```{r}
starwars$homeworld
```

8. Use mutate to create a column transforming kg to pounds. (hint: you may need to look up the conversion)

#Part 2
10. open the billboard dataset.
```{r}
data("billboard")
```

11. are the data in this dataframe in long or wide format? explain how you know.
```{r}
#The data are wide format because it is organized by each week from Week 1 to 76 in each column.
```

12. change the data from its original format to the other version.
```{r}
billboard_long<- pivot_longer(billboard, cols = wk1:wk76, names_to = "week", values_to = "score")
billboard_long
                              
```

13. change it from your altered version in #3 back to its original state.
#I do not understand what this question asks. But I will change it to wide format again.
```{r}
billboard_Wide_Again<- pivot_wider(billboard_long, id_cols = c("artist", "track", "date.entered"), names_from = "week", values_from = "score")
billboard_Wide_Again
```

14. Separate the date entered column into three columns: one for year, one for month, and one for day.
```{r}
separate_date.entered<- separate(billboard_Wide_Again, date.entered, into = c("year", "month", "day"), sep = "-")
separate_date.entered
```
